From this agreement is the saying of one of the Companions(4): ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾ (al-Mu'minun 23:14), and the Qur'an was revealed with it as he had said it.

And the Prophet (ﷺ) said about Surah al-Rahman: "I recited Surat al-Rahman to your brothers the jinn, and they responded better than you did; every time I recited ﴿Then which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾ (al-Rahman 55:13), they said: 'None of Your blessings, our Lord, do we deny; to You belongs all praise.'"(5)

So: when we hear the words of Allah, we must be moved by them, and respond to them with conscious responsiveness: at the verse of glorification we glorify, at the verse of praise we praise Allah, and at the verse of supplication we say: "Amin." These are emotional states upon hearing the Qur'an and responding to it, not that we hear it or recite it hastily like poetry.

(1) Said by Ibn 'Abbas and Sufyan al-Thawri, as transmitted from them by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/370). al-Nahhas said: this is preferable, because the Qur'an was revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ), and everything in it is addressed to him, peace be upon him, except what its meaning cannot be valid for anyone other than him. (Quoted by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir 7/5103).
(2) Bawwa'ahu: caused him to dwell; bawwa'ahu fi al-ard: established him therein. Tabawwa'tu al-manzil: I took the dwelling as a residence. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/88).
(3) Cited by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (7/5105) that the Prophet (ﷺ), when he recited this verse, would say: "Rather, Allah is better and more enduring, more majestic and more generous." Al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/370) and attributed it to Abd ibn Humayd from Qatada, "that he used to..." without mentioning its attribution to the Prophet (ﷺ).
(4) He is 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "My Lord agreed with me in four matters: this verse was revealed, ﴿And We certainly created man from an extract of clay﴾ (al-Mu'minun 23:12), and I said: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾, and it was revealed, ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾ (al-Mu'minun 23:14)." Mentioned by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (3/241) and attributed to Ibn Abi Hatim.
(5) Cited by al-Suyuti in "al-Durr al-Manthur" (7/690) and attributed to al-Tirmidhi, Ibn al-Mundhir, Abu al-Shaykh in al-'Azama, al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah (may Allah be pleased with him).
(6) Al-hadh (with dhal): rapidity of recitation. In a hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, a man said to him: "I recited al-Mufassal last night," and he said: "Is it like the hadh of poetry?" He meant: do you hurry through the Qur'an in this way, as you hurry in reciting poetry? (Lisan al-Arab, root h-d-dh).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 27, verse 60:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿Is He not (better) who created the heavens and the earth, and sent down for you water from the sky, so that We caused to grow with it gardens of delightful beauty, whose trees you could never have made grow? Is there another god with Allah? Nay, they are a people who deviate.﴾ [60]

"Is He not (better)..." [60] (An-Naml). This is another interrogative. It is as if the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, after decreeing defeat for the disbelievers and victory for the believers, wanted to nurture faith in Allah within the soul, and that they should take from Allah's granting victory to the believers a store of faith and fresh spiritual states, a powerful charge that drives them so that they themselves are prepared to confront the enemies of the call and those who oppose it.

He says, glorified is He:

﴿Is He not (better) who created the heavens and the earth, and sent down for you water from the sky, so that We caused to grow with it gardens of delightful beauty, whose trees you could never have made grow? Is there another god with Allah...﴾ [60] (An-Naml)

So then: the matter does not stop at a battle in which the believers triumphed over the disbelievers. There is in the creation of Allah something greater than that. For if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would say, "Allah." And if you asked them, "Who created them?" they would say, "Allah." These are matters they cannot deny. It is as if the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, is saying to them: Is it Allah who created the heavens and the earth and sent down for you water from the sky... or what you associate (with Him)?

Since Allah, glorified is He, has claimed the matter of creation for Himself, and no contender has risen to this claim, it has been established for Him, glorified is He, until someone else claims it: ﴿Is there another god with Allah...﴾ [60] (An-Naml). If there were another god who created the creation, then where is he? Either he was unaware of this claim, or he was aware of it and shrank from the confrontation. In both cases he is not fit to be a god. Otherwise, let him come with a creation and miracles greater than what we have seen.

So when Allah, exalted is He, says, "I am Allah, and there is no god but Me, and the whole creation, with its heavens and its earth, is My handiwork," and no opponent appears, the matter is settled for Him. Therefore He, glorified is He, says:

﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god but He, and the angels and those of knowledge... [18]﴾ (Aal 'Imran)

So the matter of Divine Oneness: Allah first bore witness to it for Himself, then the angels and those of knowledge among the creation bore witness to it.

He, glorified is He, says, affirming this meaning:

﴿Say: If there were gods with Him, as they say, they would surely have sought a way to the Lord of the Throne.﴾ [42] (Al-Isra)

That is: those gods would have banded together and risen against the God who took their dominion from them and claimed it for Himself; or they would have gone to Him to draw near to Him and seek His favour.

As for His saying, ﴿and sent down for you water from the sky﴾ [60] (An-Naml): "sky" is everything that is above you and shades you. Water is known to descend from the clouds, and the clouds are of what is above us. Or it may be that "sending down" means the willing of existence, and the willing of existence in a thing is its coming to be from the sky. Do you not see His saying:

﴿We sent down Our messengers with clear proofs, and sent down with them the Book and the Balance, that people may uphold justice.﴾ [25] (Al-Hadid)

And His saying:

﴿And We sent down iron, wherein is great might and benefits for people...﴾ [25] (Al-Hadid). It is known that iron comes from the earth, but the willing of its existence comes from the sky.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿then We caused to grow with it gardens of delightful beauty...﴾ [60] (An-Naml). Water has many benefits in our lives; indeed it is the basis of life. Therefore the verse confined itself to mentioning gardens, because they are the sustenance of human life in food and drink.

If you say: we now regard beautiful gardens as a matter of luxuries, and they contain nothing of the essentials of our lives. We say: yes, that is so now, but in the past they used to call every cultivated land enclosed by a wall a "garden" (ḥadīqa) or "enclosure" (ḥā'iṭ).

And He said ﴿of delightful beauty﴾ [60] (An-Naml), although if you look at wheat, for example, which is the mainstay of sustenance, you will find it less beautiful than the rose, jasmine, and jasmine-like blossoms, for instance. It is as if your Lord, mighty and majestic is He, is saying to you: I have undertaken the luxuries and the beautiful things; so, by greater right, I will provide you with the necessities.

The Truth, blessed and exalted is He, wishes to elevate the taste and feelings of His servants. Read, for example, His saying: ﴿Look at its fruit when it bears fruit and ripens [99]﴾ (Al-An'am). That is: before you eat of these fruits, reflect on their beauty and their wondrous appearance. It is as if this is a call to refine the general taste and to contemplate the marvellous making of Allah.

Do you not see that Allah, exalted is He, permitted you to look at all the fruits so that you might behold their beauty, and did not permit you to eat except from what you own? Therefore He said: ﴿Look at its fruit...﴾ [99] (Al-An'am). If you do not own it, then looking at it is enough for your enjoyment.

From this aesthetic elevation is His saying, after He had spoken of the necessities concerning livestock: ﴿And for you in them is beauty when you bring them home in the evening and when you send them out to pasture﴾ [6] (An-Nahl).

And He said: ﴿And horses, mules, and donkeys, for you to ride and as adornment...﴾ [8] (An-Nahl).

Thus our Lord, mighty and majestic is He, has given us the necessities of life, and has given us its luxuries and its beauties. And consider the precision of expression in ﴿Is He not (better) who created the heavens and the earth...﴾ [60] (An-Naml). The pronoun in ﴿created﴾ is the third-person pronoun (He), referring to Allah, mighty and majestic is He, and likewise in ﴿and sent down﴾. But in ﴿so We caused to grow﴾ He turned away from the third-person pronoun to the first-person plural pronoun (We), which denotes magnification. Why?

They said: because among Allah's blessings are things in which man has no part, such as creation and the sending down of rain. Such matters admit of no doubt of human participation. But there are things in which man has a part, such as tilling and growing. He ploughs, sows, waters... and so on, which may suggest that man is the one who causes plants to grow. Therefore He, glorified is He, wished to remove this illusion, so He explicitly attributed the causing of growth to Himself, mighty and majestic is He, to remove this doubt.

And your Lord, glorified and exalted is He, honours your effort and mentions your striving, saying: ﴿Have you considered what you sow? Is it you who make it grow, or are We the growers?﴾ [63–64] (Al-Waqi'a). Yes, you have action and striving in this matter, but you used the earth created by Allah, the iron implement created by Allah, the seeds created by Allah, and the water created by Allah. As for the growing itself, you have no part in it. So do not say "I planted," for We are truly the growers; rather say, "I ploughed and I watered."

Therefore you find the response at the end of the verse negating any doubt that you have a share in the matter of sowing: ﴿Were We willing, We would make it debris...﴾ [65] (Al-Waqi'a), and the verb is emphasised with the emphatic lam to negate this doubt.

In contrast to the discourse about water, where you have no share, the same verb comes, but without the emphatic lam: ﴿Have you considered the water you drink? Is it you who sent it down from the clouds, or are We the senders? Were We willing, We would make it bitter; so why do you not give thanks?﴾ [68–70] (Al-Waqi'a).

As for the meaning of ﴿Nay, they are a people who deviate﴾ [60] (An-Naml): justice ('adl) is known to be a quality of praise. When you hear ﴿Nay, they are a people who deviate﴾ [60], you may think it is a good quality in them, but such a term requires careful examination, since it carries many meanings. We say: "'adala fī kadhā" means he was equitable in such-and-such; "'adala ilā kadhā" means he inclined to it; "'adala 'an kadhā" means he left it and turned away from it; and "'adala bi kadhā" means he equalised it (with something else).

So the meaning here of ﴿yaʿdilūn﴾ [60] is turning away from Him, and would that they merely turned away from Him! Rather, they turn away from Him to something else, and make others equal to Him, as He, glorified is He, said elsewhere:

﴿Praise belongs to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light; yet those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord.﴾ [1] (Al-An'am)

That is: they make others equal to Him, glorified is He.

1. "Aynaʿ al-thamar yayna'u": it ripened, matured, and its time for picking came. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/373).
2. al-Ajaj: intensely salty water. "Ajja al-ma' yaujju": its saltiness intensified. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/7).

Then the Almighty says:

﴿Is not He who made the earth a place of settlement, and made rivers within it, and made for it firm mountains, and placed between the two seas a barrier? Is there a god with Allah? Nay, most of them do not know.﴾

When the Almighty spoke in the previous verse about the heavens and the earth, He mentioned things common to both: rain descends from the sky, the earth receives the water, and it makes gardens of delight grow for us.

As for this verse, the discourse is about the earth, so He mentions matters specific to the earth. ﴿Who made the earth a place of settlement...﴾ (al-Naml 61). The meaning of qararan (a place of settlement) is stability: He created it in a comfortable form suitable for man to settle upon.

﴿And made rivers within it﴾ (al-Naml 61). Water descends from the sky, and whoever it falls upon benefits from it directly. As for what descends upon the mountains, it gathers in the valleys, and dams are built for it so that people may benefit from it in times of drought. And some of the rainwater flows in channels called rivers.

You can distinguish between a river and an artificial canal. The water in a river flows from the high mountains and from scattered places, following the depressions and the plains of the earth, where the water can carve its course. You see it winding and meandering, turning around mountains or rocks to carve its path.

As for an artificial canal, you see it in a straight line, unless its route is obstructed, for example, by one of the people of influence, who then compels them to change the course and divert it so as to avoid passing through his land.

You can observe this phenomenon if you urinate on sandy ground and look at the path of the urine: you see it moving in a winding way according to the nature of the land it passes over.

﴿And made for it firm mountains﴾ (al-Naml 61). Al-rawasi (the firm mountains) are the stable, fixed mountains. In another place, the Almighty explained the wisdom behind these mountains, saying: ﴿And He cast into the earth firm mountains lest it should shake with you﴾ (al-Nahl 15).

The wisdom in creating the mountains is to stabilize the earth so that it does not tremble. Had it been created in a state of stability and firmness, it would not have needed mountains. Therefore, it was created in a state of motion, and weights were necessary.

The wisdom in creating the mountains is not limited to stabilizing the earth; they have another function, as the Almighty says: ﴿And the mountains He set firm, as a provision for you and your cattle﴾ (al-Nazi'at 32-33).

How can the mountains be a provision for humans and animals? Yes, they are a provision, because they are reservoirs of water. When the rain ceases, we find the water that fell upon the mountains, either in the rivers, in waterfalls, behind the dams between the valleys, or in springs and wells, from what the earth has absorbed.

Just as the mountains are reservoirs of water, they are also reservoirs of fertility that replenish the cultivated land year after year in measured amounts, so that the fertility of the land continues. We have previously spoken about the phenomenon of erosion, which crumbles the upper layer of rocks; it descends into the valleys with the rainwater and mixes with the agricultural soil, increasing its fertility.

Had the mountains not been hard and their rocks not cohesive, they would have crumbled within a few years, and we would have lost the source of fertility thereafter. This phenomenon is among the signs of God's mercy toward His creatures, because it corresponds with population growth, such that as the population increases, the fertile area suitable for cultivation increases.

We have said before that when you contemplate the arrangement of mountains and valleys, you find that a mountain is a triangle with its base downward and its peak upward, whereas valleys, contrary to mountains, are triangles with their base upward and their peak downward. Thus we see that every increase of silt from the mountain and of the alluvium (1) that crumbles from it increases the area of the valley, so the fertile area grows every year with the increase in population.

Therefore the Almighty says about the mountains: ﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days, and set up equals to Him? That is the Lord of the worlds. And He placed in it firm mountains above it, and blessed it, and measured in it its sustenance...﴾ (Fussilat 9-10).

Thus He made the firm mountains the storehouses of sustenance, of food and drink. And you may reflect on the Nile of Egypt and its valley: how it is formed from the silt carried by the waters from the high mountains of Africa, so as to make this fertile region in Egypt.

Then the Almighty says: ﴿And placed between the two seas a barrier﴾ (al-Naml 61).

The two seas: that is, the sweet and the salt, because water is of two kinds, sweet and salty. By His power and wisdom, He placed a barrier between them, although the salt water is the source of the sweet water. Therefore, Allah the Exalted made the surface area of salt water three-quarters of the surface of the earth, and the wider the surface of the water, the wider the evaporation that forms the clouds, so that sufficient rain falls for the livelihood of the earth's inhabitants.

How beautiful is the saying of the praising poet:

He presents to his noble assembly, and he presents to it only what he has acquired of his favours,
Like the sea, the clouds pour rain upon it, and it has no favour over them, for it is of their water.

And so that you may know God's favour upon us in sending down rain and providing sweet water, consider the cost and hardship you endure to distil a few centimetres of water, while you are unaware of the vast process of distillation that waters the lands and the people in every part of the world.

We have illustrated the matter of the vastness of the sea's surface by a cup of water: if you spill the water onto the ground, it dries in a few minutes, but if you leave the water in the cup for several days, very little of it decreases.

Among the sweet water is what Allah the Exalted has channelled as springs within the earth, so that man may draw it when water is scarce on the surface; or He channelled it as springs in the earth, meaning that the sweet water flows alongside the salt water without the one mixing with the other, despite the known property of water to seep through.

This is among the wonders of the power of the Creator: from the depths of the salt sea, springs of sweet water emerge, because each of them has its own path, course and channels in which it flows, such that neither oppresses the other, as the Almighty said:

﴿He released the two seas, meeting together. Between them is a barrier which they do not transgress﴾ (al-Rahman 19-20).

Just as sweet water seeps into the depths of the earth to form wells and springs, so too salt water seeps into the depths of the earth, so that from its reactions precious stones are formed, such as marble, and minerals such as iron, manganese, granite, and so on.

After mentioning these verses concerning the earth, He brought this interrogation: ﴿Is there a god with Allah?﴾ (al-Naml 60), meaning: who created these things? ﴿Nay, most of them do not know﴾ (al-Naml 61). Those who do not know, We have informed them, and We have cut off their argument by their lack of knowledge.

If we look at the earth, we will find other signs in it, beyond being a place of settlement and dwelling. The earth is dense, and there is a dusty hue in it that is not pure white; this is because Allah the Exalted wants it to receive the heat and light of the sun so that vegetation may benefit from them. Had the earth been transparent, reflecting light and heat, vegetation would not have benefited from it. Therefore we find that some crops grow in summer and others in winter.

When they conducted some experiments on plants, placing a plant in a dark place and then making a hole on one side so that light could enter, they found that the plant, by the instinct the Creator placed in it, turns towards the light to take its share of illumination and warmth. Glory be to Him who created and proportioned, and who determined and guided.

Among the signs of Allah in the creation of the earth is that He made it in a state of motion and rotation, so that every region receives its share of heat and cold, and the climate varies between summer and winter, and autumn and spring. These are cycles required by the foundations of life.

Therefore you find botanists dividing the agricultural zones of the earth, saying: this is the wheat belt, for example, and this is the banana belt, and this is the potato belt. Each belt becomes suited to a particular type of crop that matches the people of that region, its environment and its climate.

Thus you find that each type of crop in its appropriate place is not afflicted by pests, whereas when it is transferred to a place other than its own and an environment other than its own, it is bound to be afflicted.

In the earth there is another property directly related to man. Among the properties of the earth, which is from the clay from which man was created, it is in reality his first mother. When he dies, he has no refuge but the embrace of his mother, when those closest to him and most attached to him abandon him; then the mother receives him, embraces him, and conceals from him everything that would grieve him.

Among the properties of the earth is that it absorbs the waste of humans and animals and their refuse, and transforms it, by Allah's power, into fertilizer by which crops flourish and the yield increases. In the countryside, they carry the dung of animals with its foul smell to the fields, and from it there grows a beautiful, fragrant rose that people long to smell.

These are wonders of creation, which none can accomplish but Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Do you remember the proverb that says: "So-and-so makes sherbet out of fesikh (fermented fish)"? Thus is the power of God, which brings forth opposites.

Do you not see that the finest fruit we eat now comes from the Yellow Mountain in Egypt, and it is irrigated with sewage water?

(1) Al-ghareen: the silt carried by a torrent which remains on the surface of the earth, moist or dry. Al-Asma'i said: al-ghareen is when a torrent comes and settles on the earth, and when it dries you see a thin layer of mud on the surface of the earth, cracked. (Lisan al-Arab, root: gh-r-n).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 27, verse 62:

After Allah, exalted is He, has spoken of these general manifestations that all creation needs in the heavens and the earth, the mountains and the rain... etc., He, glorified is He, now speaks of particular matters that one person needs and another does not, and at one time and not another. He, glorified is He, says:

﴿Is He not (best) who responds to the distressed one when he calls upon Him, and removes evil, and makes you successors on the earth? Is there a god with Allah? Little do you remember.﴾ [27:62]

(Yujib) Response (ijabah) is the fulfilment of what is sought by the one who calls. Al-mudtarr (the distressed one) is the one who has exhausted the means and taken them, but they have not availed him. So there is nothing before him but to leave the means and turn to the One who causes the means to act, glorified is He, and so he turns to Him. That is because the Creator, mighty and majestic is He, before He created man, created for him the requirements of his life and its necessities, and subjected them to his service.

Therefore there came in the sacred hadith: "O son of Adam, I created all things for your sake, and I created you for My sake, so do not busy yourself with what is for you at the expense of that for which you were created."

Then Allah created for you the capacity by which you can harness these things, and He guaranteed you the necessary sustenance of water and plants. If you wish to make your life comfortable, then move about in life by means of the causes created by Allah and by the active energy within you, and think how to advance and enrich the movement of life around you.

The water that flows inside the house when you open the tap, the light that shines as soon as you press the electricity switch, and the car that carries you in a few minutes... all of these are advancements in the movement of people's lives, because they applied their minds to what Allah gave them of matter, intellect and thought as causes. All of this is the outstretched hand of Allah to His servants, and it is not proper for us to reject it.

So if you try and do not succeed, and the causes do not bear fruit for you, then you must turn directly to the Causer, glorified is He, because He is your Creator and the one who takes charge of you.

Recite His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side, or sitting, or standing... [10:12]﴾ (Yunus). Would that he, at the hour he calls upon his Lord and turns to Him and He answers him, would have a return to his Lord, and he would expect that harm would befall him again; but if Allah removes it from him, he quickly returns to how he was.

﴿But when We removed his harm, he passed on as if he had never called upon Us against a harm that touched him. Thus the excessive were made to see as fair what they used to do.﴾ [10:12] (Yunus)

﴿Is He not (best) who responds to the distressed one [27:62]﴾ (al-Naml). So the distressed one must surely be answered by Allah. Whoever says, "I called, but I was not answered," then know that he was not truly distressed. A hardship that passes over the servant is not of the category of necessity, such as one who asks Allah to dwell in a better residence than the one he is in, or for a salary and income greater than what he takes... etc. These are all matters in which there is no necessity, and perhaps Allah knows that they are best for you, and if He increased you beyond this measure, you would transgress and become arrogant.

As the Truth, glorified is He, said: ﴿Nay, indeed man transgresses, when he sees himself self-sufficient [96:6-7]﴾ (al-Alaq).

You sought good from your own point of view, while your Lord knows that there is no good in it: ﴿And man prays for evil as he prays for good, and man is ever hasty [17:11]﴾ (al-Isra').

So your Lord corrects this error in your understanding of matters and says to you: I will bring you good, but by another way more suitable than this one. If I answered you in what you want, something would happen whose outcome you would not praise, as though Allah, mighty and majestic is He, who is our Lord and the one who takes charge of our affairs, placed a control upon our supplications. If Allah, glorified is He, were a functionary who fulfilled each one's request, He would not deserve to be a god, far be Allah from it.

Man by nature is hasty and impetuous, so the Lord must intervene in His servant's decrees with what sets him right, and choose for him what suits him, because He, glorified is He, is the most knowing of the consequences of things and of their appropriate time, and for everything with Him, exalted is He, there is an appointed time and a birth.

Recite the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And if Allah were to hasten for people the evil as they hasten for the good, their term would surely have been decreed for them [10:11]﴾ (Yunus).

Do you not see that some mothers love their child and feel compassion for him, and if he disobeys her in something or annoys her, she raises her hands to the sky and says, "My God, let me drink your fire," or "My God, let me be blind and not see you"? So what if Allah answered this foolish woman?

Thus, from His mercy towards us, He chooses for us what is good for us of supplication, and protects us from folly and haste.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and removes evil [27:62]﴾ (al-Naml). Just as none answers the distressed one but Allah, none removes evil but Allah. If there were another god who answered the distressed one and removed evil, people would turn to him in supplication. But when a person is afflicted, he says nothing but "O Lord," and he finds no one other than Allah to turn to, because he will not deceive himself in a state of hardship or the calamity that has struck him.

We have illustrated this, and to Allah belongs the highest similitude, by the barber of health in the past, who used to do the work of the doctor now. When a son of the village graduated from the faculty of medicine, all eyes turned to him, and the barber would disparage medicine and doctors, claiming they had no experience, so that his standing among the people of the village would remain. But when the barber's son fell ill, what did he do? He could not deceive himself even if he deceived people: he took the boy in the darkness of night, wrapped him in a blanket, and went with him to the new "doctor."

Therefore every distressed person and everyone who has been struck by evil says: "O Lord, O Lord." Even the non-believer must say it, and must turn his eye and heart to the sky, to the true God, for the time is serious and admits no bargaining.

Then He says after it: ﴿and makes you successors on the earth [27:62]﴾ (al-Naml), meaning: some of you succeed others in it, as He said: ﴿He will surely make them successors in the earth, as He made successors those before them [24:55]﴾ (al-Nur).

So who possesses these matters but Allah? ﴿Is there a god with Allah? [27:62]﴾ (al-Naml). The interrogative here denies the existence of a god other than Allah who does this. ﴿Little do you remember [27:62]﴾ (al-Naml), meaning: if you had reflected and remembered, you would have known that there is no god but

Allah.

1 Ibn 'Abbas said: it is the one in dire need, the one under compulsion. Al-Suddi said: the one who has no power and no strength. Dhu al-Nun said: it is the one who has cut off his attachments from what is other than Allah. (Cited by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir 7/5107.)

Then Allah, glorified is He, says:

﴿Is He not better who guides you in the darknesses of the land and the sea, and who sends the winds as glad tidings before His mercy? Is there a god with Allah? Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him.﴾ (27:63)

This too is among the matters specific to some people rather than others, and it was so before the advance of knowledge, when the stars were the signs by which sailors at sea and travelers on land were guided: ﴿And by the stars they are guided﴾ (16:16) (an-Nahl).

Scholars from among the Arabs excelled in the sciences of astronomy (falak) and the stars, and in the sciences of the sea, and they laid foundations for these sciences. This was not from knowledge they had in themselves, but from observation of the phenomena of the universe, and by the success and guidance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

When we reflect on the ascent of human beings in life, we find that it is the result of an observation that happened by chance, or even by error. Otherwise, how did a human come to know how to leaven dough so that bread comes out in this form and with this taste? For this reason they call unleavened dough (ʿajīn) "faṭīr," which is the flat dough that has not fermented, and "khamīr," which is the dough that has fermented, risen a little, and had air penetrate it.

They also transferred this meaning to opinion. They say: "So-and-so's opinion is faṭīr," meaning superficial and hasty, and "a fikra mukhtamira" (a fermented idea), meaning studied carefully. From the same root comes "al-fiṭra," meaning a thing when it is in its natural state.

Perhaps one of the women discovered this matter of leavening through error or chance when she kneaded the dough and delayed baking it until it fermented; when she baked it, it came out in this form that we love. Likewise is the discovery of penicillin, for example, and submarines, steam, the wheel... etc.

Consider, for example: why do we cook molokhiya (jute leaves) and not cook mint? Indeed, it is then the guidance of Allah, who created and proportioned, and who determined and guided.

We learned how to work iron after putting it into fire so that it becomes soft, because Allah the Exalted taught it to His Prophet Dawud, peace be upon him, when He said ﴿And We softened for him the iron﴾ (34:10) (Saba').

Thus, much of the discoveries of the universe and its advancements come by the guidance of Allah. As time passes, the secrets of the universe are revealed to us, each in its appointed time and birth which Allah willed: either people deduce it through premises when its time comes, or else it comes even by chance.

And read, if you wish, the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And they do not encompass anything of His knowledge except what He wills…﴾ (2:255) (al-Baqarah). So when Allah wills, He reveals things to you and facilitates their causes for you; and if you do not pay attention to them, He shows them to you by chance. Among the means by which Allah makes His creatures aware, for example, are the people of the desert: you see one of them reclining, looking at the sky, and he says to you: "The sky will rain after so many hours," though there is no cloud or overcast in the sky indicating rain; but he knew it through induction and experience.

And of this divine guidance is that you see the dumb animals eating by instinct: they eat dry grass, and do not eat, for example, green mint or basil, even though its fragrance is pleasant. Why? Because He made the pleasant smell, but its taste is not pleasant. When an animal eats and is satisfied, it can never eat afterward at all, unlike the human who eats until satiety, then sweet, cold and hot foods, and they say: "Look at the colors of the food and it will show you the corners," meaning: look at your stomach, the colors and varieties of food, and it will show you its empty corners.

For this reason you find the dung of animals less disgusting than the smell of human waste, because they eat by the instinct which Allah placed in them, while we eat by appetite, and without a system we commit ourselves to.

As for His saying, ﴿And who sends the winds as glad tidings…﴾ (27:63) (an-Naml): meaning, heralds of rain. ﴿Before His mercy…﴾ (27:63): and rain is a manifestation of the mercy of Allah. ﴿Is there a god with Allah…?﴾ (27:63) (an-Naml): meaning, there is no god but Allah, who guides you in the darknesses of the land and the sea, and there is no god but Allah who sends the winds that bring you good news of rain. ﴿Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him﴾ (27:63) (an-Naml): He is far above having any partner in His dominion.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 27, verse 64:

Then the Truthful One (al-Haqq), glory be to Him, says:

﴿Is not He who originates creation, then repeats it, and who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? Is there a god alongside Allah? Say: "Bring your proof, if you are truthful."﴾

This matter of creation is one they cannot deny, and Allah has asked them: ﴿And if you asked them who created the heavens and the earth, they would surely say, "Allah..."﴾ (al-Zukhruf 43:87).

And in another place: ﴿And if you asked them who created the heavens and the earth, they would surely say, "Allah..."﴾ (Luqman 31:25).

Because they cannot deny it. And if they deny it, the answer is ready: "Let the One who created first show us something new of His creation."

The meaning of ﴿originates creation﴾ (al-Naml) is: the first creation from non-existence. ﴿Then repeats it﴾ (al-Naml): because the One who created us from non-existence has decreed death upon us, and has informed us of the unseen that we will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection, and this creation will be repeated again. Those who could not deny the creation denied the resurrection, and they said, as the Qur'an relates: ﴿Qaf. By the glorious Qur'an. Nay, they wonder that a warner has come to them from among themselves, and the disbelievers say, "This is an astonishing thing. When we have died and become dust—that is a far return."﴾ (Qaf 50:1-3)

So they considered the resurrection after death, and the dissolution of bodies into dust, far-fetched. This question has been discussed at length by the philosophers. In response to them we say: in man-made laws you give reward to the one who does good and punishment to the one who falls short, you criminalize certain specific acts and set appropriate penalties for them. In law there is: no penalty except by criminalization, no criminalization except by a text, and no text except by promulgation.

We have not seen in man-made law a crime left without punishment. So if mankind sets down for its societies these laws that organize their lives, is not the Lord of mankind more worthy of the law of reward and punishment? And if you do not accept for yourself that a criminal should escape punishment, how do you accept that for Allah?

Then do you not know that many criminals commit their crimes while the law is heedless, or they blind themselves to justice and flee punishment, and escape man-made laws in this world? If we also left these without punishment in the Hereafter, they would be the winners, and we would thereby encourage every deviant who strays from the law.

As for one who knows that he has a Lord who watches over him, and that if he is blinded to the judgment of the earth he will not be blinded to the judgment of heaven, and if he escapes the punishment of this world he will never escape the punishment of the Hereafter—if he knows this, he will be upright.

But what is the basis of their rejecting the resurrection? ﴿That is a far return﴾ (Qaf 50:3).

They say: suppose a man died and was buried, and his body dissolved into elements which the earth absorbed. Then a tree was planted in that place and nourished by these elements, and several people ate of its fruits, and particles of the dead man passed into the fruits and then into those who ate them. When creation is resurrected on the Day of Resurrection, to which of them will these particles belong: to the first or to the second? If I restore them to the first, they are a deficiency in the second; and if I restore them to the second, they are a deficiency in the first.

This speech of theirs proceeds on the basis that the person is merely matter. But the individual is matter and meaning. Suppose a stout man weighing, say, a hundred kilograms was struck by an illness that wasted him until his weight fell to fifty kilograms, for example, then he was treated and his health improved until he returned to his former state. Are the particles that were lost from his weight the same ones that entered him through health and nutrition? Certainly not. Has his personality changed through this loss or this gain? No, he is still himself.

So: the person has particles of differing composition, and has meaning and spirit; at the moment these things are gathered together, the intended person comes into being.

Therefore the Exalted says, responding to these philosophizers: ﴿We already know what the earth diminishes of them, and with Us is a preserved Record.﴾ (Qaf 50:4)

So why do you consider re-creation after death far-fetched, when you have acknowledged the first creation and confessed that Allah is the Creator? Is not re-creation from existence easier than creation starting from non-existence? Moreover, re-creation requires power to bring forth and knowledge.

As for knowledge, the Truthful One, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿We already know what the earth diminishes of them, and with Us is a preserved Record﴾ (Qaf 50:4). That is: He knows your weight and knows your particles; not a single atom of them is hidden.(1)

As for power, you have believed in it when you acknowledged His power, exalted be He, to create from non-existence, and re-creation is easier than the first origination: ﴿And He it is who originates creation, then repeats it, and that is easier for Him...﴾ (al-Rum 30:27).

Although the Mighty and Majestic should not be described as "easy" or "easier," these are used according to your understanding and to bring the matter closer to your minds.

Also regarding power, the Truthful One, exalted be He, says: ﴿Were We then wearied by the first creation?...﴾ (Qaf 50:15).

Then the Truthful One says: ﴿And who provides for you from the heaven and the earth...﴾ (al-Naml 27:64).

Rizq (provision): everything from which one benefits. It is either from the heaven, or from the earth, or from the meeting of the two, when water descends from the sky and mixes with the soil of the earth, and vegetation emerges.

﴿Is there a god alongside Allah?...﴾ (al-Naml 27:64) repeats the same earlier interrogation to affirm that there is no god but Allah, who brings you these blessings.

﴿Say: "Bring your proof, if you are truthful."﴾ (al-Naml 27:64) That is: bring the evidence for the existence of another god who says, "I am the One who originated creation, and I am the One who provides from the heaven and the earth." If no one comes to say this, then the claim belongs firmly to its owner, since no opponent has arisen. Set aside this matter of re-creation: it suffices that one claims creation, for the One able to create is able to re-create; it is not impossible for the One who created from non-existence to repeat from something existing.

But what is the connection between speaking of provision from the heaven and the earth after the matter of re-creation? There must be a relation between them. The provision that comes through the meeting of rain-water with the soil of the earth, which is vegetation, has a cycle like the human cycle and a repetition like his repetition: man feeds on the plants of the earth and takes from them his need of energy and nourishment, and what remains of it comes out as waste that decomposes in the earth; even what remains of it in the human body decomposes after death into the elements of the earth.

So the rose, for example, after its freshness, softness and beauty, when it is plucked, dries and its water evaporates; likewise its color and fragrance in the atmosphere; and what remains of it as dry matter decomposes in the soil. Then if we plant another rose, it feeds on the elements in the soil and on the color and fragrance in the atmosphere.

So: the elements of composition in the universe have neither increased nor decreased since Allah created creation, and the cycle of plant life in nature has a beginning, an end and a return, much like the creation of man, then his death, then his restoration on the Day of Resurrection.

It is as though the Truthful One, blessed and exalted, gives us evidence for re-creation through what we see of the cycle of plants: a proof, by what we see, of the unseen that we do not see.

1 Ibn 'Abbas said regarding the words of Allah, ﴿We already know what the earth diminishes of them...﴾ (Qaf 50:4): what the earth eats of their flesh, hair and bones. Qatadah said: it means the dead, whom the earth eats when they die. (al-Durr al-Manthur fi al-Tafsir bi al-Ma'thur by al-Suyuti, 7/590).

Then the Truthful One, glorified is He, says:

﴿Say: None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah, and they do not perceive when they will be resurrected.﴾ (27:65)

As the Almighty says: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He...﴾ (6:59) (al-An'am).

Al-ghayb (the unseen) is everything that is hidden from your perception and senses. But sometimes the unseen is relative (ghayb idafi), hidden from you but not from others. For example, I do not know what is in your pockets, but you know. Likewise, when something is stolen and the thief hides it, the one robbed does not know where it is, but the thief does.

Or the unseen is absolute (ghayb mutlaq), that which is hidden from all of us. It has two kinds. The first is hidden from all of us, yet we may discover it, like all the discoveries humanity has reached. These have preliminaries that lead to them, and this is a semi-relative unseen, because it is unseen today but becomes visible afterward, and so ceases to be unseen.

An example is a geometry exercise we give to children, with premises and given data, in which they exercise their minds until they reach the required solution. Of this type Allah says: ﴿And they do not encompass anything of His knowledge except what He wills...﴾ (2:255) (al-Baqarah).

When Allah wills and the birth of this unseen comes, Allah makes them aware of the preliminaries that lead to it, either through research or even by chance. This is confirmed by His saying: ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth...﴾ (41:53) (Fussilat).

From the absolute unseen is the true unseen, which none discloses or knows except Allah, for He alone is independent and unique in knowing it. Of this unseen Allah says: ﴿The Knower of the unseen; He does not disclose His unseen to anyone, except whom He has approved of among messengers...﴾ (72:26-27) (al-Jinn).

From this absolute unseen is the matter of the Resurrection. ﴿Say: None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah...﴾ (27:65) (an-Naml). The time of the Resurrection is known only to Allah, the Glorified, though He has placed for it preliminaries and signs that indicate it and announce its nearness.

He said about it: ﴿I almost conceal it...﴾ (20:15) (Ta-Ha). Some (1) think that ﴿akhfīhā⁠﻿﻿...﴾ (20:15) means: I conceal it and hide it. But the meaning is not so. ﴿Akhfīhā⁠﻿﻿...﴾ (20:15) means: I remove its concealment (2). There is a difference between khafiya al-shay' and akhfāhu: khafiya al-shay' 'anni means it was hidden from me, it covered and concealed itself; but akhfāhu means he revealed it. This is called the hamzah of removal, like a'jama al-shay' meaning he removed its obscurity. From this comes al-mu'jam, which clarifies the meanings of vocabulary.

Just as removal is done by the hamzah, it is also done by doubling the letter. We say marida fulan, meaning he fell ill, and marrada fulanan, meaning he treated him and removed his illness. From this: qashsharat al-burtuqalah, meaning he removed its peel.

So the meaning of ﴿akhfīhā⁠﻿﻿...﴾ (20:15) is: I almost reveal it. Do you not see that the Hour has major signs and minor signs, some of which we see now, and with the passing days one sign after another becomes manifest to us?

Yet the Resurrection retains its appointed time, which only Allah knows. Therefore He says of it: ﴿None reveals it at its time except Him...﴾ (7:187) (al-A'raf).

The Prophet ﷺ took pride in not knowing its appointed time, so when asked about it he said: "The one asked about it is no more knowledgeable than the one asking" (3).

Thus it is an honour for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ not to know what Allah has reserved for His own knowledge, and the Resurrection is an absolute unseen whose keys Allah has not given to anyone, not even the messengers.

Allah may honour some of His creatures and inform them of part of the unseen. Among these are the unseen matters that the Prophet ﷺ reported without there being any preliminaries leading to them, so they must have come to him through the revelation of the Qur'an, as in His saying: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land, but they, after their defeat, will overcome within a few years...﴾ (30:1-4) (ar-Rum).

The Romans were closer to Allah because they were People of the Book, while the Persians were disbelievers who worshipped fire. Therefore the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions wished for the victory of the Romans over the Persians. Then revelation came to the Messenger of Allah informing him: ﴿The Romans have been defeated⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿...﴾ (30:2), but in the end ﴿they will overcome⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿...﴾ (30:3). Had Allah not specified their victory ﴿within a few years...﴾ (30:4), their victory would have been permanent. But who can determine the outcome of a battle between two great powers after a few years, except Allah?

And because the Romans' victory delights the believers in Allah, He, glorified, said: ﴿And on that day the believers will rejoice in Allah's victory...﴾ (30:4-5) (ar-Rum).

And Allah's power willed that the Romans' victory over the Persians came on the same day that the believers triumphed over the disbelievers at Badr (4).

Among the unseen that Allah bestows upon one of His servants is what happened to al-Siddiq Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him. He had given his daughter 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, some wealth. When death approached him, he said to her: "Bring me what you have of wealth. Indeed, there are only your two brothers and your two sisters." Her two brothers are Muhammad and 'Abd al-Rahman, and her two sisters: we know of no sister of 'A'ishah except Asma', so who is the other (5)?

Al-Siddiq had married the daughter of his maternal aunt (6), and she was pregnant. But the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, manifested to him and inspired him that she would bear a girl who would join 'A'ishah and Asma' (7).

As for His saying: ﴿and they do not perceive when they will be resurrected⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿...﴾ (27:65): just as we do not perceive death nor know its appointed time, likewise we do not perceive the resurrection, nor when we will be raised.

1 Said by Ibn 'Abbas, as transmitted by Ibn Abi Hatim and cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (5/563): "I will not reveal it to anyone but Myself..."
2 Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn al-Anbari reported from Warqa' who said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr recited to me (akād akhfīhā) with a fatha on the alif, meaning: I reveal it. (al-Durr al-Manthur, al-Suyuti, 5/563).
3 A hadith agreed upon. Muslim recorded it in his Sahih (8), and al-Bukhari in his Sahih (50), from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab: Jibril, upon him peace, came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the form of a man asking him, among what he asked: "Tell me about the Hour." He said: "The one asked about it is no more knowledgeable than the one asking." He said: "Then tell me of its signs." He said: "That the slave-girl gives birth to her mistress, and that you see the barefoot, naked, destitute herdsmen of sheep competing in building tall buildings." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to 'Umar: "O 'Umar, do you know who the questioner was?" I said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "That was Jibril, who came to teach you your religion."
4 From Abu Sa'id al-Khudri who said: When the day of Badr came, the Romans prevailed over the Persians, and the believers were pleased by the Romans' prevailing over the Persians. Recorded by al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 197.
5 She is Umm Kulthum bint Abi Bakr al-Siddiq al-Taymiyyah, a Successor. Her mother was Habibah bint Kharijah, who bore her after Abu Bakr's death. Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah al-Ansari narrated from her (al-Isabah 8/276).
6 She is Habibah bint Kharijah ibn Zayd al-Khazrajiyyah, wife of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and mother of his daughter Umm Kulthum, whom Abu Bakr died leaving in her womb. He said: "The one in the belly of Kharijah's daughter, I do not think it is anything but a female," and so it was. After Abu Bakr's death she married Isaf ibn 'Utbah ibn 'Amr. See al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah (8/48).
7 Abu Bakr al-Siddiq married several women:
Umm Ruman bint 'Amir ibn 'Uwaymir al-Kinaniyyah, by whom he had 'A'ishah and 'Abd al-Rahman.
Its name was Zaynab bint 'Ubayd: she was the wife of al-Harith ibn Sakhbarah or of 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, and bore him al-Tufayl. Then he died and her ally Abu Bakr al-Siddiq married her. She died during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ (al-Isabah 8/232).
Habibah bint Kharijah, by whom he had Umm Kulthum, and she remarried after him.
Qutaylah bint 'Abd al-'Uzza, a Qurashi woman from Banu 'Amir ibn Lu'ayy, the mother of Asma' and 'Abd Allah. Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani said in al-Isabah (8/169): "If she lived until the conquest, then it is apparent that she embraced Islam."

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿Rather, their knowledge of the Hereafter has followed on (i.e., been continuous). Rather, they are in doubt concerning it. Rather, they are blind to it.﴾ (66)

The meaning of ﴿ادارك﴾ (idaraka) in the verse (An-Naml, 66) is: tadarak, i.e., it followed on and continued in succession. The talk of the Hereafter came continuously from all the Messengers, and from this is the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿until, when they had all overtaken one another therein﴾ (Al-A'raf, 38), meaning: some of them gathered upon others.

So, the announcement of the Hereafter came in succession from every one of Allah's Messengers. None of them was sent without calling to faith in Allah and the Last Day, and bringing the proof for it.

And despite the continual reminder of the Hereafter, Allah said of them: ﴿Rather, they are in doubt concerning it﴾ (An-Naml, 66), i.e., concerning the Hereafter. So why? He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Rather, they are blind to it﴾ (An-Naml, 66), i.e., their eyes and their insight were blinded to it, so they were not guided. Had their eyes and hearts been opened, they would have believed in it.

He, exalted is He, says: ﴿For indeed, it is not the eyes that go blind, but it is the hearts within the breasts that go blind﴾ (Al-Hajj, 46).

So there is something that truly exists, but I have neglected it, or I have deliberately ignored it. The signs of resurrection and the Day of Judgment exist and have been continuously present, but people were blind to them and so did not see them.

The meaning of ﴿عمون﴾ ('umun) in the verse (An-Naml, 66) is the plural of ('amm), which is one whose insight has become blind to the clear evidences of the Resurrection.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And those who disbelieve say: "When we have become dust, and our fathers, shall we indeed be brought forth?"﴾

They wish to infer from the non-resurrection of the fathers the non-resurrection of themselves. But who told them that the Hereafter (al-akhirah) would come together with this world? The Hereafter is only so named because it comes last (ākhiran), after the world has come to its end.

We have been promised this, we and our fathers before us. This is nothing but the fables of the ancients. (68)

That is, since the time of Adam (peace be upon him), people have been dying, and the prophets have been reminding them of this Last Day, yet it has not happened. "This is nothing but the fables of the ancients": that is, falsehood, fabrication, and the weaving of fancy, as in the tales of earlier peoples. But what is it that drives them to accuse the Messengers, in their conveying of God's message, with this charge?

They say: because a person's own self is dear to him, and everyone who is extravagant against his own soul through sins wants to secure his self and ease it. He has no comfort except by saying that this speech is a lie, or by wishing that it were a lie. Even if he acknowledged the Resurrection, the Resurrection and the Reckoning, his calamity would be great, for there is nothing in his store but disbelief in God and disobedience to His commands. How, then, would he acknowledge the Resurrection? It is natural that he would comfort his self by denying what the Messenger reported.

Therefore we find some of these people saying about predestination: "If God has decreed disobedience for me, why does He punish me for it?" Logic would require that they complete the picture and say: "And if He has decreed obedience for me, why does He reward me for it?" Why do you mention the evil and neglect the good?

So these people seek an escape route by which they can flee the consequences of their deeds.

God, exalted is He, calls them to travel through the regions of the earth to observe and reflect, not on those who were raised, for the resurrection has not yet come, but to observe the end of the criminals who denied their messengers in what they brought, and how God defeated them, drove them away, and decreed victory for the messengers.

Resurrection (al-ba'th) is among the things the messengers brought. Whoever denies the messengers denies resurrection, although it is a certain reality without doubt. But the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, conceals its time, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿It is not for anyone but Him to reveal it at its time...﴾ (al-A'raf, 7:187).

Then Allah, exalted is He, consoles His Messenger ﷺ so as to lighten the grief he bears in the course of the call, so He says:

﴿And do not grieve over them, and do not be in distress because of what they plot.﴾

Allah, glorified is He, has also addressed His Messenger in His words:
﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over their following him, if they do not believe in this message, in sorrow.﴾ (Al-Kahf)

The meaning is: destroying yourself through grief. Al-Bakhʿ (bakhʿ, violent slaughter), as we have said, is excessive cutting in slaughter to the point of reaching the bakhaʿ (al-bakhaʿ, the spinal marrow).(1) Allah, blessed and exalted is He, makes clear that the Messenger's task is only to convey the message from Allah; he is not responsible for whether one believes or disbelieves. Rather, the Prophet's ﷺ love for his community and his eagerness for its salvation made him grieve and suffer when even one of his community strayed from him. Did not his Lord say of him:
﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves; it grieves him that you suffer, he is anxious over you, to the believers he is kind and merciful.﴾ (At-Tawbah)

(1) Al-Zamakhshari said: It is from bakhaʿa al-dhabiḥa (بخع الذبيحة), when one exaggerates in slaughtering it, which is to cut through the bone of its neck and let the slaughter reach the bakhaʿ (with the letter bāʾ), which is the vein in the backbone; whereas al-nakhʿ (with the letter nūn) is short of that, namely to let the slaughter reach the nukhāʿ, which is the white thread running through the neck. Ibn al-Athir said: This is how al-Zamakhshari mentioned it in al-Kashshaf and in his book al-Faʾiq fi Gharib al-Hadith, and I have not found it in anyone else's work. (Lisan al-Arab, root: b-kh-ʿ)

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says concerning them:

﴿And they say, "When will this promise be, if you are truthful?"﴾ 71

Those who deny the Resurrection say: ﴿When will this promise be...﴾ 71 (al-Naml), that is, the Resurrection, ﴿if you are truthful﴾ 71 (al-Naml) about there being a resurrection.

They called God's informing them of the Resurrection a "promise," even though it is in fact a threat against them. There is a difference between wa'd (promise) and awʿada (threat): wa'd is used for good, and iw'ād is used for evil. But God Almighty obliterates their tongues, and they are people of eloquence, so they say ﴿When will this promise be...﴾ 71 (al-Naml), which for them is a threat, because a warning from one who opposes you is, in effect, bad news, just as a promise from one who opposes you is good news.

It is as if the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, is saying: We have made promises concerning two matters. We promised Our messengers support and victory, and We promised the whole world the Resurrection. So if We are truthful in the first, which you witness and perceive with your senses, then take it as a premise and as evidence of Our truthfulness in the second. You have seen that all the messengers prevailed over their deniers, either by the punishment of total annihilation or by the punishment of defeat and humiliation.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿Say: "Perhaps some of what you are hastening for will come close behind you."﴾

The word عسى ("perhaps" or "it may be") indicates hope, but when it comes from God it indicates certainty. If you said, for example, "Perhaps so-and-so will give you," the hope would be weak. It would be stronger if you said, "Perhaps I will give you, because I do not control so-and-so, but I control myself." It would be stronger still if you said, "Perhaps God will give you, because my own means may not enable me to fulfil it." When God Almighty says عسى, however, it is the utmost assurance and certainty in hope, and the highest and most emphatic degree of it.

The meaning of ﴿ردف لكم﴾ ("come close behind you") is: follow you and come after you. It derives from أردفه, meaning to make someone ride behind you on a mount, so that he is directly behind you. And indeed, what they were hastening for did befall them. It was not long before defeat overtook them at Badr.(1) Thus We confirmed in the first case what We had said: ﴿The multitude will be routed and they will turn their backs﴾ (54:45), which you have witnessed. So take this as evidence of the unseen that We told you about.

(1) Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (7/5114): "﴿Some of what you are hastening for﴾ (27:72) refers to the punishment, and that was the Day of Badr. It was also said: it refers to the punishment of the grave."

Then the Lord of Might, glorified is He, says:

﴿And indeed your Lord is full of bounty toward mankind, but most of them do not give thanks.﴾ [27:73]

From His bounty toward you is that He delays the Resurrection, so that people may take heed; for otherwise He would have seized them suddenly from the very first denial. This shows that Allah gives respite to creation so that the people of guidance and faith may increase among them. Do you not see that the believers in the Messenger of Allah did not come all at once, at one time, but over wide spans of time?

Therefore we have said: the early Muslims, in their battles against disbelief, would grieve if one of the heads of disbelief and its leaders escaped their killing, such as Ikrimah, Amr, Khalid and others. Had Allah shown them the Unseen, they would have known that Allah had delivered them from their hands in order to keep them for later, to support Islam, and to be among its leaders and among its swords drawn against the faces of the disbelievers.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But most of them do not give thanks﴾ [27:73] is evidence that some of them do give thanks.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And indeed your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they disclose.﴾ (27:74)

You may say regarding this verse: If God, may He be exalted, knows what their breasts conceal and what they hide, then by greater priority He knows what they disclose, so why did He say after it: ﴿and what they disclose﴾ (al-Naml)?

We say: Because what is in the breasts is unseen (ghayb), and God is unseen (ghayb). And someone may say: since God is unseen, none knows the unseen except God. We reply to him that God, may He be exalted, knows the unseen and knows the seen (al-'alan).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 27, verse 75:

The meaning of ﴿ghā'ibah... 75﴾ (al-Naml): it means "the hidden thing" (al-shay' al-ghā'ib), and the ta' indicating intensification (al-mubālaghah) has been attached to it, just as we say, in intensive form: rāwin and rāwiyah, nassāb and nassābah, 'ālim and 'allāmah. Likewise ghā'ib and ghā'ibah, intensifying its hiddenness.

Some hold that min ("from") here is superfluous (zā'idah), but the word "superfluous" does not befit the style and eloquence of the Noble Qur'an, and we exalt the speech of Allah above filler (ḥashw) and vain talk (laghw) that has no meaning. Others, showing courtesy toward the Qur'an, said that min here is ṣilah (a connecting particle), but a connecting particle for what?

Therefore it must have a meaning that we should clarify. We say: if you wish to deny that you have any money with you, you say: "mā 'indī māl" (I have no money), meaning that you have no money of significance, though it does not preclude that you may have, for example, a few piasters which are not called money. But if you wish to deny money in the sense of establishing generality in the soul, you say: "mā 'indī min māl", meaning: starting from anything that is called money, however small. So min here is neither superfluous nor a connecting particle; rather it is for the beginning of the limit (lil-ghāyah) and the establishing of generality in negation.

Thus the meaning of ﴿And there is not a hidden thing in the heaven and the earth but that it is in a clear Record. 75﴾ (al-Naml) is that Allah, exalted is He, has His knowledge encompassing everything from eternity, however small it is and of no account. Read His saying, exalted is He:

﴿And not a leaf falls but He knows it, nor a grain in the darkness of the earth, nor anything moist or dry, but it is in a clear Record. 59﴾ (al-An'am).

Likewise His power, exalted is He, does not stop at the limit of knowledge; rather He also records it ﴿but in a clear Record. 75﴾ (al-Naml), that is, in the Mother of the Book (Umm al-Kitab), in which Allah has recorded all the events of the universe. So when the events come, we see them conforming to what Allah recorded about them from eternity. For example, when the Truthful, blessed and exalted is He, mentioned the means of transport and travel at the time of the Qur'an's revelation, He said: ﴿And horses, mules and donkeys for you to ride, and as an adornment; and He creates what you do not know. 8﴾ (al-Nahl).

Were it not for the verse's conclusion with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and He creates what you do not know. 8﴾ (al-Nahl), there would be an objection against the Qur'an. For where are the car, the airplane and the rocket among the means of transport?

Therefore: we can now bring all modern means under ﴿and He creates what you do not know. 8﴾ (al-Nahl).

We have already said: among the greatness of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, is that He does not know of a thing in which the servant has no choice, but He knows what is within the servant's choice and exposes him by his choice, as happened in the matter of the change of the qibla: ﴿The foolish among the people will say: "What has turned them from their qiblah which they used to face?..." 142﴾ (al-Baqarah).

Allah openly declares it and names them foolish, because they oppose Allah and oppose the Messenger of Allah. After this enmity and this disparagement, they indeed said what the Qur'an related of them.

We have not seen among them a sensible person who reflects on this verse and says: "Since the Qur'an has related this about us, we will not say it." In that case they would have been permitted to accuse the Qur'an and to impugn its truthfulness and the standing of the Messenger of Allah. But that did not happen; after the revelation of the verse they indeed said: ﴿what has turned them from their qiblah which they used to face...142﴾ (al-Baqarah), meaning: they abandoned facing Bayt al-Maqdis and turned toward Makkah. They said it while possessing reason and choice.

This matter also occurred regarding Abu Lahab, when Allah said of him:

﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he! 1 His wealth and what he earned will not avail him. 2 He will burn in a Fire of blazing flame. 3﴾ (al-Masad)

Because he said to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, when he gathered them to convey to them the call of Allah: "Ruin to you! Is it for this that you gathered us?"(1) Abu Lahab was the uncle of the Messenger of Allah, like Hamzah and al-'Abbas, and the Messenger of Allah did not know the future of his uncle; perhaps he would believe as Hamzah believed and became the lion of the Messenger of Allah, and as al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib believed.

When ﴿Perish the hands... 1﴾ (al-Masad) was revealed, he was able to deny it and to believe, uttering the two testimonies even hypocritically; he had the capacity for that, and he had choice in it, but he did not do so.

Therefore: among the greatness of the words of Allah and among the aspects of its inimitability is that it passes judgment upon a choosing disbeliever, and it is a Qur'an recited openly before the heads of the witnesses, yet he cannot confront it, and the Qur'an remains the proof of Allah against every disbeliever and obstinate one.

When we reflect on His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We will be its guardian. 9﴾ (al-Hijr), we see that the Truth, glorified is He, sent down the Qur'an and undertook its preservation Himself, exalted is He, and did not entrust it to anyone, although in the Qur'an there are things and events that have not yet occurred. It is as if Allah takes upon Himself their preservation, recording them and announcing them, why? Because they will certainly happen.

The Truth, glorified is He, does not fear that the reality of things may not obey Him, because He is their Owner. Do you not see that a person preserves the bill of exchange that is owed to him and does not concern himself with the one that is owed by him? As for our Lord, mighty and majestic is He, He preserves for us things while they are owed by Him, glorified and exalted is He.

And read, if you wish: ﴿The multitude will be routed and they will turn their backs. 45﴾ (al-Qamar). So Allah records them upon Himself and preserves them, because He is able to bring them about; and indeed the multitude was routed and they turned their backs, and Allah spoke the truth.

(1) On the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When ﴿And warn your nearest kindred. 214﴾ (al-Shu'ara') was revealed, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, went out until he ascended al-Safa (a hill in Makkah), and they gathered to him. He said: "Tell me, if I informed you that a cavalry was about to emerge at the foot of this mountain, would you have believed me?" They said: "We have never found you to be a liar." He said: "Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment." Abu Lahab said: "Ruin to you! Is it for this that you gathered us?" Then this surah was revealed: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he! 1﴾ (al-Masad). Narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (2/181), Ahmad in his Musnad (1/307), Muslim in his Sahih, Kitab al-Iman (hadith 355), and al-Bukhari in his Sahih also (8/736 - Fath al-Bari).

The difference is between addressing someone whose mind is blank and addressing someone who already holds a preconceived idea. The blank-minded person accepts what you say, whereas the one with a preconceived idea opposes you. Likewise, among the disbelievers and the People of the Book there are those who oppose the Book of God and deny what it brought. Although they are enemies of Islam and hate it, if you ask them about what the Qur'an has reported, they say: "Yes, we know this from our books." ﴿So when there came to them that which they recognised, they disbelieved in it; so the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers﴾ (al-Baqarah 2:89).

Therefore, when our master ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam (1) looked at the Messenger of Allah, he knew that he was the true Messenger, and his soul inclined to Islam, and he said: "By Allah, I recognise Muhammad as I recognise my son, and my recognition of Muhammad is even stronger." And God spoke the truth when He said of them: ﴿They recognise it as they recognise their own sons...﴾ (al-Baqarah 2:146).

ʿAbd Allah knew that Islam is the path that leads him to God, the path every intelligent person should follow. When he wished to embrace Islam, he wanted to win the round by announcing his Islam and exposing the hypocrites, the disbelievers and the People of the Book. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, my soul has aspired to Islam, and I fear that if I embrace Islam the Jews will disparage me and do such-and-such to me. So ask them about me before I embrace Islam." The Messenger of Allah asked them, and they said: "He is our scholar and the son of our scholar... " and they showered him with praise and commendation. When ʿAbd Allah said: "Now that you have said what you have said, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah," they said: "Rather, he is our evil one and the son of our evil one," and they heaped upon him expressions of abuse and insult (2).

(1) Abu Yusuf ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam ibn al-Harith, of the descendants of the Prophet Yusuf (peace be upon him). He was from the Banu Qaynuqa. His name had been al-Husayn, and the Prophet (ﷺ) named him ʿAbd Allah. He embraced Islam when the Prophet (ﷺ) first arrived in Madinah; it is also said that his Islam was delayed until the eighth year (AH). He was the most knowledgeable of the Children of Israel and one of their leaders. He died in Madinah in the year 43 AH. (al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah 4/81).

(2) Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (8/165, Fath al-Bari) and al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (2/527-529) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him). In some wordings of the hadith, they first said: "That is our master and the son of our master, and our most knowledgeable and the son of our most knowledgeable," and in another wording: "Our best and the son of our best, and our master and the son of our master."

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, describes the Qur'an, saying:

﴿And indeed, it is guidance and mercy for the believers﴾ [27:77]

The meaning of ﴿guidance﴾ is guidance by way of indication and direction, and this applies to both the believer and the disbeliever. As for ﴿mercy﴾, it is for the believers only, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers...﴾ [17:82]. There is a difference between healing and mercy, because the conjunction here requires difference. Healing is from the disease which the Qur'an came to treat, and mercy is that this disease does not return to you again.

Then Allah, glorified is He, says:

﴿Indeed, your Lord judges between them by His decree, and He is the Mighty, the All-Knowing.﴾

As for His words, ﴿the Mighty... [78]﴾: that is, the One who overpowers and is not overpowered, who prevails and is not prevailed upon, and whose protection cannot be violated. And He is, in addition to that, in His might, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾. For a being may be mighty and unconquerable, yet have no knowledge. Allah, however, is Mighty and All-Knowing; He places might where it belongs and places humiliation where it belongs.

As He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Say, "O Allah, Owner of sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will and remove sovereignty from whom You will. You elevate whom You will and You debase whom You will. In Your hand is [all] good.﴾ [Ali 'Imran 26]

The scholars paused at His words concerning Himself: ﴿In Your hand is [all] good﴾ [Ali 'Imran 26]. Some of them exerted their reasoning and said: the implied wording is "In Your hand is [all] good and evil." This interpretation indicates a failure to grasp the meaning of the verse, for what is with Allah is good in every circumstance. Granting sovereignty to one who acts justly toward his subjects is good, and removing sovereignty from one who tyrannises with it and oppresses is also good, since Allah strips from him the instrument of tyranny so that he does not persist in it. Thus, goodness is present in everything.

Since among His attributes, exalted is He, is that He is Mighty, All-Knowing, Merciful, and Possessor of bounty, then be assured, O believer in Allah, and put your trust in Allah.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿So put your trust in Allah. Indeed, you are upon the clear truth.﴾ [27:79]

Tawakkul (complete reliance upon God): that you feel your own weakness in a matter you try to accomplish by your own strength, and you find no such strength within you. True tawakkul is only upon Allah, the Ever-Living who does not die. As for if you place your trust in a human being like yourself, he may be overtaken by death before he fulfils your need.

And His saying ﴿Indeed, you are upon the clear truth﴾ (An-Naml): that is, you rely upon Allah while you are upon the truth and upon obedience to Him, mighty and majestic is He, not upon His disobedience. And as long as you rely upon Allah while you are in a state of obedience, He will certainly be your helper and supporter.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, consoles His Messenger (ﷺ), so that he does not grieve over those who turned away from him and did not believe:

﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call when they turn away, retreating.﴾ [27:80]

The meaning: Do not grieve, O Muhammad, and do not destroy yourself over these people of your nation who did not believe. Your duty is only to convey (al-balagh). Conveying is a speech that has a receiving instrument in the listener, which is the ear. When this instrument is disabled, they will not hear. These people have had their instrument of hearing disabled, so they are like the dead and like those afflicted with deafness. The signs of God in the cosmos are abundant around them, yet they do not see or hear.

Would that the matter stopped at deafness. Rather, they turn their backs in retreat from hearing the call, and this is an exaggeration on their part in turning away from the call of truth; for if they sat down they still would not hear, so what of when they turn their backs, running far away? It is as if each one of them fears that his deafness might be cured and his ear might catch the call of God, so that the call would sway him, and then his calamity would be great, by their own reckoning.

This is evidence that they know it is the truth, and that if they were to lend it an ear they would follow it. Did they not say: ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during it...﴾ [41:26]?

That is because the Qur'an has a majesty and beauty that captivates hearts; therefore they forbade its hearing and called for creating disturbance around it, so that it would not reach the hearts.

1 Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (7/5117): "This verse has been contrasted with the story of Badr, with the greeting upon graves, and with what has been related in that regard, that the spirits are at the edge of graves at certain times, and that the dead hears the sound of sandals when people leave him, and other things. Had the dead not heard, the greeting would not be made upon him." He also said in his book al-Tadhkira (p. 164): "There is no contradiction between them, because it is permissible that they hear at a certain time or in a certain state, for specifying a general statement is possible and valid when a specifier is found, and it has been found here." Or the intended meaning is the negation of hearing that benefits them.

Then the Truthful One, glorified is He, says:

﴿And you cannot guide the blind away from their error. You can only make heard those who believe in Our signs, and they are Muslims.﴾ [27:81]

There is a difference between hearing a statement of truth or a matter of veracity while your mind is empty, and hearing it while your mind is occupied with its opposite. So in order for hearing to bear fruit, you should receive the call with an empty mind, and then examine the call with your intellect along with what contradicts it. Whatever your soul is drawn to and at peace with, admit it.

This is what they call, even in material matters, the "theory of space" (nazariyyat al-hayyiz), meaning that a single space cannot hold two things at the same time. I had previously given an example of this with a bottle: when you fill it with water, the air must first come out in the form of bubbles, because water is denser than air.

As for the meaning of ﴿You can only make heard those who believe in Our signs, and they are Muslims﴾ [27:81]: someone may say, "Since you make heard only those who believe in Our signs, what is the benefit of hearing when they are already believers?"
