We say: the signs are three, arranged one upon another. The first is the cosmic signs of belief (al-ayat al-kawniyya al-'aqadiyya), which you witness in the universe and by which you infer the existence of a Creator God who is capable. Then you ask: who is this Creating God? Here comes the role of the Messenger, who explains to you and solves this riddle for you. And there must be with him signs that demonstrate his truthfulness in conveying from God, which is the miracle (mu'jiza). If we neglect the cosmic signs, the Messenger reminds us of them, saying: "And among His signs is such-and-such."

When you believe in the cosmic signs and the signs of miracles, then you must believe in the signs of the legal rulings (ayat al-ahkam) that the miracle of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, brought.

Then Allah, glorified is He, says:

﴿And when the word has fallen upon them, We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth, speaking to them that mankind did not have faith in Our signs.﴾ (27:82)

The word "waqa'a" (fell, came to pass) here means "saqata" (fell down). It falls by its own nature, and needs no one to force it to fall. And the falling "upon them" is as in His saying, ﴿So the roof fell upon them from above them﴾ (16:26).

The word "waqa'a" here indicates that they will encounter hardships and troubles. By tracing this root (waqa'a) in the Qur'an, we find that it always occurs in the context of hardships, except in one place, which is His saying, ﴿And whoever leaves his home as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger and then death overtakes him, his reward has already become incumbent upon Allah﴾ (4:100).

And since they did not listen to the signs, did not accept them, did not pay attention to the method of Allah, and closed their ears to it, and did not hear the speech of their like among mankind, We will bring forth for them a creature that will speak to them.

﴿We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth, speaking to them﴾ (27:82). Consider this humiliation and this rebuke: you did not listen to the speech of your own kind among mankind, and you did not understand the one who addressed you in your language. So listen now to the lowly one, understand from it, and interpret its words.

But what will the creature say to them, and what is the nature of its speech? ﴿That mankind did not have certainty in Our signs﴾ (27:82). That is: they did not believe in Our previous signs. Here I am speaking to them, and it is incumbent upon the skilled among them to say to me: how should I speak to him?

People have differed concerning this creature (2), and concerning its form and attributes, and how speech comes from something outside the familiar kind of speech, namely a creature? But since Allah, the Exalted, has informed us of it, it is true and must not be opposed. We must accept that what the Qur'an reports as having occurred before it came to pass is evidence of its truthfulness regarding what it reports about what is yet to occur.

(1) The word "waqa'a" occurs in the Qur'an seven times:
Five of them mean the falling and descent of punishment and hardship: (al-A'raf: 71, 134), (Yunus: 51), (al-Naml: 82, 85).
Two places: one is what the honored Shaykh mentioned (al-Nisa' 100). The second is His saying, ﴿So the truth came to pass and what they used to do was nullified﴾ (al-A'raf 118), meaning: the truth was established.

(2) Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (7/5119): "There has been great disagreement about the identity of this creature, its description, and where it will emerge from.
First: it is the young camel of Salih's she-camel, and this is the most sound, Allah knows best, as mentioned by Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi in his Musnad from Hudhayfah.
Second: it is reported that it is a hairy, bristly creature with legs sixty cubits long.
Third: it is said that it is the Jassasah, the saying of Abdullah ibn Umar.
Fourth: it is reported from Ibn Umar that it is in the form of the children of Adam, and it is in the clouds while its legs are on the earth.
Fifth: it is reported that it was made up of the features of every animal."
Al-Qurtubi said: The difficulty concerning this creature has been removed by what we have mentioned from the hadith of Hudhayfah, so let reliance be placed upon it." That is: that it is the young camel of Salih's she-camel.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 27, verse 83:

﴿And [remember] the Day when We shall gather from every nation a company of those who denied Our signs, and they will be marshalled in order.﴾ 

Al-fawj (the company): they are a group and a throng of people. The first to be gathered on that standing are the obstinate and the tyrants who undertook to deny the signs of Allah. God gathers them first in front of the common folk, leading them and running ahead of them toward the Fire, as He, glorified is He, said about Pharaoh: ﴿He will lead his people on the Day of Resurrection and bring them down to the Fire...﴾ (Hud 98).

Just as he led them astray in the world, he leads them to the Fire in the Hereafter. When the misguided see their imam in misguidance leading them, their hope of salvation is cut off. They may have clung to him in this standing, expecting him to deliver them, but how can he, when he is running ahead of them to this same destiny?

As for the meaning of ﴿fa-hum yuza'un﴾ (An-Naml 83): we have said, regarding the meaning of ﴿yuza'un﴾ (An-Naml 83), that it means they are held back (ya'munun), and the intended meaning is that they are held back from letting the first of them overtake the last of them, so that they all enter together. So God, blessed and exalted is He, gathers the first of them upon the last of them, so that they are made to stand together in the Fire: the follower and the followed are all equal in abasement and humiliation. Perhaps one of the obstinate or tyrants tries to get ahead so that his followers do not see him, and thus his affair is exposed, so God holds him back in order to disgrace him before the heads of all creation.

Note 1: This is the saying of Qatada as transmitted by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (7/5123), and the saying of Mujahid as cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/384), who attributed it to ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim. There is another saying: i.e., they are driven on (yusaqun), related by Ibn Zayd. Al-Qurtubi said: i.e., they are pushed and driven to the place of reckoning.

In Surah al-A'raf, the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, presents a detailed account of this situation and of this dialogue that takes place on the plain of the Resurrection. He, the Exalted, says:

﴿So who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah or denies His signs? Those will receive their portion of the Decree [of what was written for them], until when Our messengers come to them to take their souls, they will say, "Where is that which you used to invoke besides Allah?" They will say, "They have strayed from us," and they will testify against themselves that they had been disbelievers. [Allah] will say, "Enter into the fire among nations that passed away before you, of jinn and mankind." Every time a nation enters, it curses its sister [nation], until, when they have all overtaken one another therein, the last of them will say of the first of them, "Our Lord, these are the ones who misled us, so give them a double punishment of the Fire." He will say, "For each is double, but you do not know." And the first of them will say to the last of them, "You had no virtue over us, so taste the punishment for what you used to earn."﴾ (Al-A'raf)

Their word of the verse: "And the word has fallen upon them for what they did wrong" (﴿ووقع... ٨٥﴾), meaning: the punishment became due for them, ﴿for what they did wrong﴾, and it is as though it were a tangible thing falling upon their heads. ﴿So they cannot speak﴾: their tongues have been struck dumb from the terror of what they saw, so they find no speech with which to speak.

Then the Almighty says:

﴿Have they not seen that We made the night for them to rest in, and the day to see by? Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.﴾ [27:86]

The discourse moves from speaking about the Hereafter to a cosmic sign. This is one of the features of the style of the Noble Qur'an, which alternates between the call to faith and the explanation of cosmic signs. Having spoken to us about the Hereafter, He mentioned this cosmic sign, as if to say: there is no excuse for one who denies the signs of God, for the signs are present and observable.

Therefore He said: ﴿Have they not seen...﴾ [27:86], i.e., have they not known and observed, ﴿that We made the night for them to rest in...﴾ [27:86], i.e., for sleep and repose, ﴿and the day to see by...﴾ [27:86], i.e., with what it contains of rays and light that causes sight.

We have already explained the role of the Muslim scholar Ibn al-Haytham (Ibn al-Haytham, the physicist and optician) in correcting the theory of seeing objects. They used to believe that a thing is seen when a ray comes out from the eye to it. The correct view is that the ray comes out from the visible object to the eye. So the ray is what, as it were, perceives; it is the cause of sight, and without it we would not see things.

﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe﴾ [27:86]. Your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has arranged for you the movement of your life: a night in which you rest and take your repose, and a day in which you strive and seek of God's bounty, as He said: ﴿And out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein and that you may seek of His bounty, and perhaps you will be grateful﴾ [28:73].

The movement of life will not be set right for us unless we follow this order which God has chosen for us. If people reverse this natural order and stay awake until dawn, they must encounter the consequence of this violation in the movement of their lives: laziness, slackness, and low productivity, etc.

The Almighty, blessed and exalted, explains this matter to us in another place:

﴿Say: "Have you considered: if God made the night perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than God could bring you light? Will you not then listen?" Say: "Have you considered: if God made the day perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than God could bring you a night in which you rest? Will you not then see?"﴾ [28:71-72]

In speaking of the night He said: ﴿Will you not then listen?﴾ [28:71], and of the day He said: ﴿Will you not then see?﴾ [28:72]. Why? They said: because the faculty of perception at night is hearing, and during the day sight, and this is an indication of the nature of each of them, so that we do not change it ourselves, by staying up at night and sleeping by day.

In His saying, ﴿And out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein and that you may seek of His bounty...﴾ [28:73], there is what the scholars call al-laff wa'l-nashr (the figure of "folding and unfolding," i.e., mentioning two things together and then assigning each its counterpart), namely: He folded the subject of the judgment, which is night and day together, then unfolded the judgment of each in order: ﴿that you may rest therein﴾, which corresponds to the night, and ﴿that you may seek of His bounty﴾, which corresponds to the day.

So, after the Almighty had argued from the existing reality of the two signs of night and day, He wished to argue further from what follows them, in ﴿Say: "Have you considered: if God made the night perpetual...﴾ [28:71] and ﴿Say: "Have you considered: if God made the day perpetual...﴾ [28:72].

[1] Al-sarmad: a long or perpetual period of time. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/312)

[2] Al-laff wa'l-nashr: it is that two things, or several things, are mentioned, either in detail by specifying each one, or in summary, by using a word that encompasses multiple items, and then items are mentioned corresponding to that number, each returning to one of the earlier ones, leaving it to the listener's intellect to assign each to what befits it. An example of the summary type is His saying: ﴿And they say: None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews or Christians...﴾ [2:111], i.e., the Jews said: none will enter except Jews, and the Christians said: none will enter Paradise except Christians. (See the detailed treatment in al-Suyuti's al-Burhan fi Ulum al-Qur'an 3/280.)

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 27, verse 87:

Then the context returns once more to the discussion of the Resurrection:

﴿And on the Day when the Horn is blown, whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified, except whom Allah wills. And all will come to Him in humble submission.﴾ 87

It is as if Allah, exalted is He, is saying to me: turn your attention to the lesson in the cosmic signs, for they will benefit you on a coming Day, which is the Day of Resurrection. ﴿The Day when the Horn is blown...﴾ 87 (An-Naml). It is the trumpet. ﴿...whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified, except whom Allah wills...﴾ 87 (An-Naml). Al-fazaʿ (terror) is intense fear that seizes everyone in the heavens and everyone on the earth. ﴿Except whom Allah wills...﴾ 87 (An-Naml). They said: they are the angels: Israfil, who blows the Horn, Jibril, Mika'il, and 'Azra'il (2).

Therefore, when our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), spoke about this matter of the swoon, he said: "I will regain consciousness from the swoon, and find my brother Musa holding on to the Throne" (3). That is because Musa (peace be upon him) swooned once in this world when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, as the Qur'an relates: ﴿So when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble, and Musa fell down unconscious...﴾ 143 (Al-A'raf).

Allah would not combine two swoons upon His prophet Musa (peace be upon him); therefore he does not swoon the swoon of the Hereafter.

As for His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And all will come to Him in humble submission﴾ 87 (An-Naml), meaning: abased and humiliated, with none of them able to refuse Allah, since they have no power to do so, for the Resurrection ends the choice they had in this world, by which Allah had given them some dominion: ﴿Say: O Allah, Master of the dominion, You give dominion to whom You will, and You take dominion away from whom You will, and You exalt whom You will and You abase whom You will...﴾ 26 (Ghafir).

On the Day of Resurrection, everything you possess is taken from you, and every power you have over what you own, even your limbs; you have no power over them, nor any will for them to obey you. They were following your will in this world: by them you see, hear, walk and strike. But in the Hereafter this will has been taken from you, as is shown by the fact that they will testify against you and dispute on your behalf on the Day of Resurrection.

1 On the authority of Abu Hurayra, regarding His saying ﴿...whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified, except whom Allah wills...﴾ 87 (An-Naml): he said: they are the martyrs. Al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/384) and attributed it to Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn Jarir al-Tabari. Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (7/5126): "And it is the view of Sa'id ibn Jubayr that they are the martyrs, bearing swords around the Throne. The hadith of Abu Hurayra was declared sound by Qadi Abu Bakr ibn al-'Arabi, so rely upon it, for it is an explicit specification, whereas the other is ijtihad, and Allah knows best."
2 Said by Muqatil, as reported from him by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (7/5126).
3 Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (3398), and similarly by Muslim in his Sahih (2374) with similar wording, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "People will swoon on the Day of Resurrection, and I will be the first to regain consciousness; and behold, Musa will be holding onto one of the legs of the Throne, and I do not know whether he regained consciousness before me or was recompensed with the swoon of Mount Sinai."

Then the context moves us once again to a cosmic sign:

﴿And you see the mountains, you think them fixed, but they pass by as the passing of clouds — the handiwork of Allah, who has perfected everything. Indeed, He is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ (88)

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿you think them fixed...﴾ (88) (An-Naml): i.e., you suppose them to be stable and judge them to be without motion; for this reason we call them al-rawasi (the firmly set ones) and al-awtad (the pegs). ﴿...but they pass by as the passing of clouds...﴾ (88) (An-Naml): i.e., the matter is not as you suppose, for they move and pass as clouds pass, but you do not perceive this motion or notice it, because you move along with them at the same speed as their motion.

Suppose that we are in this assembly, you before me and I before you, and this mosque were on a millstone or a wheel that turns us around: would our position and situation relative to one another change?

Therefore, you cannot notice this motion unless you are outside the moving thing. Do you not see that when you ride the train, for example, you see the telephone poles running while you are stationary?

Because this phenomenon is wondrous, creation will pause before it, and Allah removes their wonder, so He says: ﴿the handiwork of Allah, who has perfected everything...﴾ (88) (An-Naml), meaning: do not be amazed, for the matter is the handiwork of Allah, His engineering, and the marvel of His creation. He chose here one of His attributes, exalted is He: ﴿who has perfected everything...﴾ (88) (An-Naml), meaning: every creation with Him is according to precise, perfected reckoning.

Some(1) understood the verse as referring to the passing of the mountains in the Hereafter, citing His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the mountains will be like wool fluffed up﴾ (5) (Al-Qari'ah).

This is incorrect, because the meaning of ﴿like wool fluffed up﴾ (5) (Al-Qari'ah) is that they will be crumbled and scattered, not that they pass by. This is one point. The other is that the speech here is built on supposition, ﴿you think them fixed...﴾ (88) (An-Naml), and there is no supposition in the Resurrection, for when it comes, all its events are certain.

Furthermore, clouds do not move by themselves, and they have no motor that moves them; rather, the wind moves them. Likewise, the motion of the mountains is not intrinsic to them, for we have never seen a mountain move from its place. Thus the motion of the mountains follows the motion of the earth, since they are pegs upon it, and the motion of a peg follows the thing into which it is driven.

Therefore, when the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, spoke of the mountains, He said: ﴿And He cast into the earth firm mountains lest it shake with you...﴾ (15) (An-Nahl).

Had the earth been created in a state of stillness, it would not have needed something to fix it; so it must be that it was created in a state of motion.

In the past, before the development of science, people did not believe that the astrologers and the unbelieving astronomers knew the unseen. But now, since scientists have reached the laws of the motion of the earth and of the other planets in the solar system, and have been able to calculate all of that with a precision that has enabled them to know the phenomenon of the eclipse of the moon and the sun, for example, and the type of each and its timing, and indeed the phenomenon occurs at the very time they specified, without deviation.

And by calculating this motion they were able to ascend to the surface of the moon, to launch space vehicles and steer them with precision, so that one of them joins another in outer space.

All these phenomena, had they not been based on certain truths, would have led to false results and failed.

Among the proofs that establish the soundness of what we incline to regarding the meaning of the motion of the mountains is that His saying, exalted is He, ﴿the handiwork of Allah, who has perfected everything...﴾ (88) (An-Naml), is a bounty from Allah through His making, and Allah does not bestow favor through His making on the Day of Resurrection; the favor is upon us now, while we are in this world.(3)

(1) Al-Qushayri said: "And this is on the Day of Resurrection." (Quoted by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir, 7/5127.)

(2) Mada yamid: to move and tremble. That is, lest it sway and convulse, for the high mountains balance the deep seas. (Al-Qamus al-Qawim, 2/246.)

(3) Al-Mawardi said in his tafsir of the verse that it is a parable, and concerning what it is a parable of there are three sayings:
First: it is a parable Allah struck for this world, in which the one who looks at it thinks it stands still like mountains, while it is taking its share of passing away like clouds; said by Sahl ibn Abd Allah.
Second: it is a parable Allah struck for faith, which you think is firmly fixed in the heart while its deeds rise to heaven.
Third: it is a parable Allah struck for the soul at the moment of the departure of the spirit, while the spirit travels toward the Throne. (Quoted by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir, 7/5128.)

This passage is linked in a subtle way to what precedes it. Just as the cosmic signs of which Allah, blessed and exalted, has informed you are a reality, and you have confirmed their truth by witnessing them yourself and perceiving them with your senses, so too we inform you now of another truth that you should accept. From the truth of what you have witnessed, take proof of the truth of what is hidden from you. Your Lord informs you that ﴿whoever comes with a good deed will have better than it...﴾ (An-Naml 27:89).

Al-hasanah (the good deed): the verb in it refers to what Allah desires in worship. If you perform the act in accordance with the will of Allah, it becomes a good deed for you. A good deed is multiplied by Allah tenfold, and it is multiplied up to seven hundred times according to the performer's capacity for sincerity (ikhlas) and devotion to Allah in his act.

The meaning: ﴿whoever comes with a good deed...﴾ (An-Naml 27:89), i.e., in this world, ﴿will have better than it...﴾ (An-Naml 27:89), i.e., something that arises from it in the Hereafter.

We hear from some people who say: if our saying "There is no god but Allah" is a good deed, then the reward for it is better than it. This statement results from an imprecise understanding of the meaning of the verse, because Allah, whom we acknowledge in the testimony, is the One who bestows this reward upon me. So whoever comes with a good deed, there is a good that arises from this good deed and is caused by it. It is like if you said: "The officer of the station is better than the Minister of the Interior": meaning, a good that came to us from his side and reached us from his direction. Is he not the one who holds the decision of appointing him?

Among this is what the people of the Sufi path and the majdhub (enraptured) say: "Muhammad is better than his Lord." In such sayings there is a toying with people's minds and stirring of their emotions, and perhaps exposure to harm. How could he say this word when Muhammad is a messenger sent from Allah? But when you consider the expression carefully, you find it correct: the speaker's meaning is that Muhammad is a good that came to us from Allah.

Or the meaning may be: ﴿better than it...﴾ (An-Naml 27:89) that the reward for the good deed is better than the good deed, because you perform the good deed as a temporary act, whereas its good and its reward will remain for you eternally without end.

Then the Truthful, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed (1), their faces will be thrown into the Fire. "Are you being recompensed except for what you used to do?"﴾ (90)

The meaning of ﴿fa-kubbat... (90)﴾ (An-Naml): they will be thrown forcefully. He singled out the faces, although all the limbs will be thrown down, because the face is the noblest and most honoured of them in the eyes of its owner, and the face is the seat of dignity and pride. Thus Allah, blessed and exalted is He, wills for them humiliation and abasement. In another place He explains that all the limbs will be thrown down into the Fire, when He, exalted, says: ﴿Then they will be thrown into it, they and the deviators﴾ (Ash-Shu'ara' 94).

This destination is not an injustice to them, nor a fabrication against them: ﴿Are you being recompensed except for what you used to do?﴾ (An-Naml 90). And as He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Today no soul will be wronged at all﴾ (Ghafir 17). So We do not favour the owner of a good deed, nor do We wrong the owner of an evil deed.

(1) That is: with shirk (associating partners with Allah). This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, al-Nakha'i, Abu Hurayrah, Mujahid, Qays ibn Sa'd and al-Hasan. Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (7/5130): "It is a consensus among the people of interpretation that the good deed is 'there is no god but Allah', and that the evil deed in this verse is shirk."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 27, verse 91:

Since Allah, exalted is He, has given us this knowledge which draws our attention to His power in His signs in the cosmos, and reminds us of the Hereafter and what it contains of reward and punishment, there is nothing for you but to commit yourself (ʿarafta fa-lzam: "once you know, then adhere"). Know that whoever conveys to you the methodology of Allah will precede you in adhering to it, for the Law is such that what He commands you, He commands me.

﴿Indeed, I have only been commanded to worship the Lord of this city...﴾ (an-Naml 91). So if I ask you to undertake any obligations, I have first demanded them of myself, because I am certain of the sincerity of my conveying from Allah; therefore I have bound myself to them.

Worship (ʿibadah), as we have said, is the obedience of the worshipper to the One worshipped in what He commands and in what He forbids, because your Lord created you from nothingness, sustained you from nothingness, and arranged for you the movement of your life. So if He imposes an obligation on you, know that the obligation is for your sake and for your benefit, because He is the Lord who takes charge of your upbringing. If you were left without a methodology, without "do" and "do not," upbringing would be deficient.

Therefore: it is part of the completeness of lordship (rubbubiyyah) that my Lord directs me just as we direct our young children and raise them, and it is part of the completeness of lordship that these commands and prohibitions exist for the benefit of the one who nurtures. Since your Lord has laid them down for you, it is necessary that you obey Him.

Accordingly, we notice in this verse ﴿Indeed, I have only been commanded to worship the Lord of this city...﴾ (an-Naml 91) that it does not say "I have been commanded to obey Allah," because divinity (ulūhiyyah) entails obligation, whereas lordship (rubūbiyyah) entails bounty and upbringing. Thus the verse clarifies the ground (ḥaythiyyah) of your hearing the ruling from Allah: that He, exalted is He, raises you through these commands and these prohibitions, and the fruit of this upbringing will return to you.

Thus, when they related to Abu Bakr the account of the Night Journey (isrāʾ) and the Ascension (miʿrāj), he did not pass the matter through his intellect, nor did he consider how true it was. Rather he said concerning the Messenger of Allah: "If he said it, then he has spoken the truth." The criterion for him was that the Messenger of Allah had said it; then he gave the reason for this, saying: "Indeed I affirm him in the news that comes from heaven, so how would I not affirm him in this?"

And Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿The Lord of this city...﴾ (an-Naml 91), that is, Makkah, and He singled it out for mention because His House is in it: ﴿Indeed, the first House established for mankind is that at Bakkah, blessed...﴾ (Āl ʿImrān 96). Then He mentions one of the attributes of Makkah: ﴿...which He has made sacred...﴾ (an-Naml 91). It is thus a sanctuary in which fighting is forbidden. This is a means of protecting the world from the corruption of wars and the corruption of disputes which lead every party to be seized by pride, so that it finds no solution but the sword.

It is as if the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, gives His creatures an opportunity for restraint and an excuse behind which they may shelter, so that they are not swept along by their delusions. When the sanctity of the place in the Sacred Precinct (al-Ḥaram) and the sanctity of time in the Sacred Months (al-Ashhur al-Ḥurum) prevent them from war, because every act must have a time and a place, and when the Law forbids them from fighting, one of them may say: "I did not refrain out of weakness; had Allah not prevented me, I would have done this and that." He shelters behind what Allah has legislated of the prohibition of fighting, until he tastes the sweetness of peace, whereupon his soul softens and yearns to return.

Because of the sanctity of Makkah, a man would meet the murderer of his father there and would not attack him, out of respect for the sanctity of the House. This sanctity has also extended to include other classes: its trees may not be cut, and its game may not be hunted.

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And to Him belongs everything...﴾ (an-Naml 91), because when Allah, exalted is He, chooses messengers from among the angels and messengers from among men, and chooses places from the earth and times, He wishes to spread selection across all things.

The Truth, blessed and exalted is He, does not show favoritism to anyone. When He sends a messenger to convey his message to all people, its benefit returns to everyone; likewise, in the sanctity of a place or a time, its benefit returns to everyone. Therefore He joined to ﴿...which He has made sacred...﴾ (an-Naml 91) the words ﴿...everything...﴾ (an-Naml 91), so the prohibition was made for the sake of these people.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And I have been commanded to be among the Muslims﴾ (an-Naml 91), that is, those who implement the methodology of Allah, meaning: I do not hold beliefs which I report but do not implement. Allah, exalted is He, has joined faith and righteous deeds, because the benefit of faith is that you act upon it, as He, exalted is He, says: ﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss, except those who have believed and done righteous deeds...﴾ (al-ʿAṣr 1–3).

Thus Allah, exalted is He, wants faith and the rulings to transfer into practical conduct within the movement of life.

1 Al-Bayhaqi related in Dalāʾil al-Nubuwwah (2/361) from the hadith of ʿAʾishah, who said: "When the Prophet (ﷺ) was taken by night to the Farthest Mosque, in the morning people were talking about it. Some who had believed in him and affirmed him apostatized, and they went to Abu Bakr and said: 'Do you have a word about your companion? He claims that he was taken by night to Bayt al-Maqdis.' He said: 'Did he say that?' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'If he said that, then he has spoken the truth.' They said: 'Do you affirm that he went to Bayt al-Maqdis tonight and came back before morning?' He said: 'Yes, indeed I affirm him in what is further than that: I affirm him in the news of heaven, in a morning or an evening.' For this reason Abu Bakr was named al-Siddiq."
2 ʿAḍada al-shajar yaʿḍuduhu, fa-huwa maʿḍud: he cut it with the miʿḍad (a cutting tool). Al-ʿAḍīd is what is cut from trees, that is, they strike it so that its leaves fall, and they take it as fodder for their camels. (Lisan al-ʿArab, root ʿ-ḍ-d.)

You, when you recite, are in reality not reciting but hearing our Lord speak. The meaning of ﴿And to recite the Qur'an...﴾ [27:92] is: keep up your intimacy with the Book with which you have been charged, so that it shows that out of your love for the one who charged you, you came to love the One who charges, and so you love to hear Him. The recitation of the Qur'an is in itself a pleasure and a delight.

So I will take pleasure from its recitation, and I will keep up the conveying of the Qur'an to people. After that, I am a model before my community, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Certainly you have in the Messenger of Allah an excellent example...﴾ [33:21].

That is: something to be followed. And since the Messenger is a role model, every station of the Messenger other than the message, whoever walks in the footsteps of the Messenger takes from it. Likewise, the place of every person in piety is according to his regard for and imitation of the exemplar. As for the message, leave that aside, for you will not take it.

The meaning of ﴿whoever is guided...﴾ [27:92] is: the guidance has reached him and he is convinced by it. ﴿Then he is guided only for his own self...﴾ [27:92], because Allah will give him help and increase him in guidance and success: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their piety﴾ [47:17].

So then: guidance and piety do not benefit the one who prescribes; rather they benefit the servant who is guided.

Then he mentions the opposite: ﴿And whoever strays, say: I am only one of the warners﴾ [27:92]. What concerns me is only that I am one of the warners, and you only go astray to your own detriment, and you bear the consequence of your straying.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 27, verse 93:

After you have completed what your Lord addressed you with, namely that you worship the Lord of this city (al-balda) and be among the Muslims, and after you have recited the Qur'an and continued to enjoy the intimacy and delight of hearing God speak, and then conveyed it to the people, when you have done all of this, praise God who enabled you to do it:

﴿And say: "Praise be to God. He will show you His signs, and you will recognise them. Your Lord is not heedless of what you do."﴾

That is: Praise be to God for His blessings and for having guided us. And praise be to God who does not punish anyone except after the proof has been established against him and warning has been delivered to him.

God will show you His signs in yourselves and in others, so you will recognise the proofs of His power, glory be to Him, and His oneness, in yourselves and in the heavens and the earth.

﴿And your Lord is not heedless of what you do.﴾ (al-Naml)

Rather, He is a witness over everything.
